items.q: You had a boy named Slick Jones... Hank Jones... Bobby Starks... And Fat Man Turner on bass, Eddie Mallory on the trumpet, and Fred -- Freddy Robinson. And a boy named Garvin Bushell... I stayed with them a long time

ctx.x: By the way, in that hand of Charlie Turner's you had some beautiful people together. You had a boy named Slick Jones, beautiful drummer, you had Hank Jones, he was the pianist, you had Bobby Starks, used to play with Fletcher Henderson. He was one of the most surprising trumpet players. You'd say, what is he doing and all of a sudden he'd find his way everytime. He'd be in some -- I would call them thickets. You'd say, how is he coming out of there. Here comes Bobby (humming). That's what it was.

And Fat Man Turner on bass, Eddie Mallory on the trumpet, and Fred -- Freddy Robinson. And a boy named Garvin Bushell, that was another post of wisdom, Bushells, talking about You see, that wisdom is always there, and I used to hang wisdom. / (Inaudible) with Bushell. And I stayed with them a long time until this altercation, and then I had to leave that and went with -- I had then I got a band of my own. / all geechies. and the band was good. This band I had was singing, a quiet singing. They sounded bad, their…

"Them asked me how I knew," what you talking, man, don't say "them" she ax him. I said, no, man. "They, asked me how I knew." And when I got finished, they were singing that stuff in unison. And it was beautiful. But we didn't get too far. Went down to a place called the Kentucky Ballroom and broadcast one night and Jimmy Lunceford or somebody got me onto there immediately.
